items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: We had Charlie Shavers, Teddy Wilson, Al Hall, Specs Powell and Trummy Young.

ctx.x: Oh, he's nice, he sure is. He was on that Mildred Bailey Show too, you know. He was always my favorite, next to Lawrence Brown. In fact, when we were in Honolulu I asked him, you know, I think, you know, like Trummy is the father of modern trombone playing in my opinion. Bill Harris and all these hotshot names and everything really got it from Trummy. And I used to get my head handed to me when I'd tell this to guys. "No, man." Et cetera.

So I told this to Trummy, I said, "How's it feel, you know, to have all these guys imitate you and everything?" He said, "I feel kind of complimented." I told him, "You know, you're really the father of modern trombone playing. I always believed Bill Harris copied you and everything." And I said, "I get my head handed to me for saying that." He said, "You know, that's true. Bill Harris told me so. He's a real nice guy and he always told me how much he appreciated, how much he'd gotten from me."
